reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. Let V:E->R be C^2, let kappa be a nonnegative real with 1<=kappa, and suppose for every x,v in E that
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Fix real eta,epsilon with 0<eta<1 and epsilon>0, a natural J>=2, and a real h>0. For i,j in Fin(J)={0,...,J-1}, define exactly
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi)),
  ell_j(X)=product_{k!=j} ((t_j-t_k)^(-1))(X-t_k),
  Lambda=sup_{s in [0,h]} sum_j |ell_j(s)|,
  omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i} (t_i-s)ell_j(s) ds,
  pw_j=omega_{J-1,j},
  bw_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s) ds.
Nodes use real coercions, polynomials use the specified inverse-denominator products, Lambda is the real interval-image supremum, and all interval integrals use real Lebesgue measure. If h^2 Lambda<=1, the following conclusions hold.
There exist global measurable p,q:E->E and N:E->N such that for every y in E,
  p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y,
  ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon,
  proximalQuery(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1),
and p is 1-Lipschitz: ||p(u)-p(v)||<=||u-v|| for every u,v in E.
The interpreter proximalQuery is the actual supplied recursive function: zero fuel gives none; positive fuel evaluates g(x) and tests ||x+eta g(x)-y||<=epsilon. If that test passes it returns (x,1); otherwise it recurses at x_next=y-eta g(x) with one less fuel, propagates failure and adds one to a successful returned count. The count includes the terminal successful gradient/residual test. N(y)+1 is a successful finite execution certificate, not a claim that N is computed without cost before execution.
Let G be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability law on E and let
  gamma=(G x G) x ((product_{Fin(J)} G) x (product_{Fin(J)} G)).
Thus gamma is the independent product of two single E-valued Gaussian vectors and two independent arrays of J E-valued Gaussian vectors, with independent array coordinates. For any f:E->E and input w=((X,P),((zeta0,zeta1),(G0,G1))), define
  a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)),
  P0=a P+sigma zeta0,
  Y0_i=X+t_i P0,
  Z0_j=grad V(f(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta)G0_j),
  Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j,
  Z1_j=grad V(f(Y1_j)+sqrt(eta)G1_j),
  Phi_f(w)=(X+h P0-sum_j pw_j Z1_j,
            a(P0-sum_j bw_j Z1_j)+sigma zeta1).
Write S=E x E. For two states (X,P),(Xprime,Pprime), define explicitly
  d2((X,P),(Xprime,Pprime))=sqrt(||X-Xprime||^2+||P-Pprime||^2).
This is the displayed position/momentum square-root sum-of-squares distance, rather than an unspecified default product-space norm. For every real rho and measures mu,nu on S, define the extended-nonnegative functional
  W_rho(mu,nu)=[inf_{pi measure on S x S: pi.fst=mu, pi.snd=nu}
                    integral^- (ENNReal.ofReal(d2(s,sprime)))^rho dpi(s,sprime)]^(rho^(-1)).
The integral is the lower integral, infimum ranges over all coupling measures with the stated marginals, and powers are real powers in extended nonnegative reals. ENNReal.ofReal embeds the nonnegative part of a real number.
There exist Markov kernels Kp,Kq from S to S, each with probability output measures, such that for every incoming state s,
  Kp(s)=(z -> Phi_p(s,z))_* gamma,
  Kq(s)=(z -> Phi_q(s,z))_* gamma.
For every s in S and every real rho>=1, including noninteger rho without any upper restriction,
  W_rho(Kq(s),Kp(s)) <= ENNReal.ofReal(3 h Lambda epsilon).
Furthermore, for every function r:E->E that is measurable and every real delta>=0 satisfying ||r(y)-p(y)||<=delta for every y in E, there exists a Markov kernel Kr from S to S such that, simultaneously for every state s,
  Kr(s)=(z -> Phi_r(s,z))_* gamma,
and for every state s and every real rho>=1,
  W_rho(Kr(s),Kp(s)) <= ENNReal.ofReal(3 h Lambda delta).
All sums use exactly the J actual indices. The witnesses p,q,N are fixed before both kernel comparisons; Kp,Kq are fixed before the universal perturbed-map statement. Each Kr works for all incoming states and all these exponents at once. The transport bounds compare one-step output laws at the same incoming state, and no incoming law, finite moment assumption, existence of an optimal coupling, stationarity, sampler convergence, mixing rate, elapsed-time guarantee or total phase-query complexity bound is asserted.
objects: Real inner-product space E; potential V,gradient,Hessian,kappa; eta,epsilon,J,h; cosine nodes t,Lagrange basis ell,interval supremum Lambda,omega,pw,bw; global measurable implicit map p,approximate map q,natural count certificate N; genuine recursive proximalQuery; Gaussian product law gamma; phase map family Phi_f; state space S=E x E with explicit distance d2; transport coupling infimum and functional W_rho; Markov kernels Kp,Kq and perturbed Kr; arbitrary measurable perturbation r and uniform error delta.

For these witnesses there exist Kp,Kq with probability outputs and pushforward identities for every state. Their bound holds for every state s and every real rho>=1. Additionally,for every measurable r and every delta>=0 with all-y uniform error <=delta,there exists one Kr with probability outputs and its pushforward identity for every state and bound for every state and every real rho>=1. Kr is not chosen separately for each state or exponent. No incoming probability-law parameter or moment assumption is quantified.
assumptions: E has all listed structures;kappa>=1 with kappa nonnegative;V is C^2;the Hessian quadratic form is bounded below by kappa^(-1)||v||^2 and above by ||v||^2 universally in x,v. 0<eta<1;epsilon>0;J>=2;h>0. The conclusion is conditional on h^2 Lambda<=1 with Lambda defined from the cosine-node Lagrange basis. No separate h<=1 assumption is stated. conclusion: There exist global measurable p,q,N with the exact implicit equation,uniform epsilon error and successful actual proximalQuery equality at fuel/count N(y)+1, and p is 1-Lipschitz. There are probability-valued Markov kernels Kp,Kq equal to gamma pushforwards of Phi_p,Phi_q for every state. For all s and real rho>=1,the explicit d2-based W_rho(Kq(s),Kp(s)) is <=ofReal(3h Lambda epsilon). For any measurable uniform-delta perturbation r of p,there is a probability-valued Kr equal to the Phi_r pushforward at every state,with W_rho(Kr(s),Kp(s))<=ofReal(3h Lambda delta) for all s and real rho>=1. All conjuncts are simultaneous for the chosen p,q,N,Kp,Kq.
scopes: The transport distance uses sqrt(||DX||^2+||DP||^2),not the default product-space norm. W is the rho-th root of an infimum of lower-integrated rho-th powers over all coupling measures with the stated marginals;attainment is not asserted. The bounds compare same-state output laws and cover all finite real rho>=1,including noninteger exponents;no finite-moment hypothesis is imposed. q and r need measurability and uniform closeness,but no Lipschitz property is concluded for either;only p is nonexpansive. The interpreter test is exactly ||x+eta g(x)-y||<=epsilon,without a (1-eta) factor. The count records actual evaluations including the terminal successful test,and N is a finite certificate without a free-precomputation claim. No kernel contraction across distinct states,mixing,invariance,total phase count or explicit joint-Phi measurability conjunct is added. No material ambiguity is present in the supplied context.
